items.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
items.summary: CERT-EU warns of two critical PHP vulnerabilities enabling unauthenticated remote code execution, fixed in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. PoCs are circulating publicly.

items.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on a critical GitLab CE/EE flaw allowing unauthenticated arbitrary code execution; prioritise internet-facing instances and assess for compromise.

items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: A critical flaw in the AMP feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write files and run commands as root; Cisco PSIRT confirms active exploitation.

items.title: Ransomware gang talked AI agents into doing much of its dirty work
items.summary: Sophos reports the Aur0ra ransomware group (GOLD OGRE) used Cursor AI coding agents with supplied VPN and proxy access to map networks, harvest credentials and reach domain admin.

items.title: New VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi AI to Rank Victims by Financial Value
items.summary: New Windows infostealer VOLTA-AUTODOXER harvests browser, Outlook and Slack data and uses LLMs (Claude, Gemini, Kimi) to rank victims by monetisation value.

items.title: Russia, Ukraine air raid alert apps hit by cyberattacks after truce ends
items.summary: Air raid alert apps in both Ukraine and Russia were hit by cyberattacks after the truce ended; Ukrainian users received fake nuclear threat warnings.

items.title: Ukraine says public air raid alert app sent false alerts after being hacked
items.summary: Ukraine confirms its public air raid alert app was hacked and sent false alerts to users.

items.title: FBI links $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist to North Korean hackers
items.summary: The FBI attributes the record $6.3 billion Binance crypto theft to North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor.

items.title: Alpine Linux rebuilds GitLab after attempted RCE attack
items.summary: Alpine Linux rebuilt its GitLab server and reset all passwords after attackers attempted to exploit the critical GitLab RCE flaw on 20-21 October.

items.title: CVSS 10.0 LXD, MicroCloud Flaw Lets Attackers Impersonate Trusted Clients Without a Private Key
items.summary: A CVSS 10.0 flaw in Canonical's LXD and MicroCloud lets attackers impersonate a trusted client using only its public certificate, granting cluster and VM access over the HTTPS API.

items.title: Hackers Steal About $2.7 Million From Polymarket Traders via Hijacked DebugBear Script
items.summary: Attackers replaced a third-party DebugBear page-speed script on Polymarket, selling signed-in traders' positions and stealing about $2.7 million; the firm is refunding 726 wallets.

items.title: FBI Links North Korea's TraderTraitor to Record $6.43 Billion Binance Crypto Heist
items.summary: FBI, USSS and IRS-CI formally attribute the $6.43 billion Binance theft to North Korea-aligned TraderTraitor (Jade Sleet/UNC4899), the largest crypto heist on record.

items.title: The first ten lines of a command policy for AI coding agents
items.summary: Interview on governing AI coding agents: giving agents their own identity, handling credential proxies, command policies and preventing data exfiltration via package installs.

items.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after record crypto hack
items.summary: Binance users withdrew $3.6bn after a record hack affecting $6.3bn in digital assets; the exchange had frozen transactions during the incident.

items.title: Russian emergencies ministry's mobile app hit by cyberattack, TASS says
items.summary: Russia's emergencies ministry mobile app was hit by a cyberattack, according to TASS.

items.title: Allies fear Trump will target NATO in case of midterm loss
items.summary: European diplomats fear Trump could cut NATO funding or withdraw further US troops from Europe if Republicans lose the midterms.

items.title: Quoting Kyle Kingsbury
items.summary: Commentary by Kyle Kingsbury arguing LLM-generated code and docs erode trust signals in software projects, raising questions on how maintainers demonstrate quality.

items.title: OneNote File Extraction, (Sun, Nov 1st)
items.summary: SANS ISC diary walks through extracting embedded files from OneNote (.one) documents, useful for malware analysis of OneNote-based lures.

items.title: NetamLoader Malware Targets Government Windows 10 Systems in Asia via .NET Injection
items.summary: Kaspersky details NetamLoader, an undocumented .NET assembly-loading framework used in a sophisticated chain against a custom Windows 10 build used by Asian government entities.

items.title: 5th EMPACT Hackathon leads to the detection of 51 potential victims
items.summary: The fifth EMPACT Hackathon in Amsterdam brought 40 investigators from 20 countries together on digital aspects of human trafficking, identifying 51 potential victims and five suspects.

items.title: Byoky: Open-source wallet for AI API keys
items.summary: Byoky is an open-source wallet storing AI provider API keys encrypted on-device, brokering requests so apps receive session tokens instead of the raw key.

items.title: Canada, coffins and confessionals
items.summary: Brussels begins defining EU-Canada 'associate membership' after the Montreal summit, with a six-month deadline set by PM Carney.

items.title: The Pentagon’s IT agency wants to bridge network gaps in the Pacific
items.summary: The Pentagon's IT agency aims to close network interoperability gaps with partners in the Indo-Pacific, per INDOPACOM's deputy commander.

items.title: Bulgaria has its first elected female president
items.summary: Iliana Iotova wins Bulgaria's presidential runoff, becoming the country's first elected female president.

items.title: Who gets to build the future of AI?
items.summary: Politico Europe piece questioning who will shape the future of AI development; no further detail in the excerpt.

items.title: North Korea says US-South Korea nuclear drill shows need for stronger nuclear deterrent
items.summary: North Korea cites a US-South Korea nuclear drill as justification for strengthening its nuclear deterrent.

items.title: ISC Stormcast For Monday, November 2nd, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10160, (Mon, Nov 2nd)
items.summary: SANS Internet Storm Center daily Stormcast podcast episode for 2 November 2026.

items.title: Binance sees outflows stabilising as exchange returns online after $6.3 billion heist
items.summary: Binance reports outflows stabilising as the exchange comes back online after the $6.3 billion theft.

items.title: EU and Canada’s 6-month test of commitment
items.summary: After the Montreal summit, 27 EU governments and Ottawa have six months to define a deeper EU-Canada partnership.

items.title: Russian strikes leave thousands without power in Ukraine, says Zelenskyy
items.summary: Zelenskyy says Russian strikes left thousands without power in Ukraine, while Moscow reported significant damage to an industrial site in Nizhny Novgorod.

items.title: OpenAI says it's doubling Pro usage limits and bringing Work features to Chat
items.summary: OpenAI is doubling Pro usage limits and bringing ChatGPT Work features into regular Chat, combining allowances across ChatGPT and Codex.

items.title: Commission backs Tusk as he vows no compromise in court showdown
items.summary: The European Commission backs Polish PM Tusk in a judicial appointments standoff, with Commissioner McGrath saying the Sejm holds the power to appoint judges.

items.title: UK’s future lies in EU, says Rachel Reeves
items.summary: Former UK chancellor Rachel Reeves says the UK's future lies with the EU, ahead of a UK-EU summit this month.

items.title: Chatbots Are Leading Hikers Astray, With Dangerous Consequences
items.summary: Wired reports chatbot-generated route planning is misleading hikers, illustrating risks of over-reliance on AI output without critical review.

items.title: How Merz’s five-day Asia trip ended up being mostly about Europe
items.summary: German Chancellor Merz's Asia trip was dominated by European security concerns, and his proposed trade alliance faces obstacles.

items.title: Week in review: Binance hit by $6.3 billion theft, impact of Brotli vulnerability
items.summary: Help Net Security's weekly roundup covers the $6.3 billion Binance theft, the Brotli vulnerability impact and open-source community pushback against AI projects.

items.title: Binance sees spike in withdrawals as exchange returns online after $6.3 billion heist
items.summary: Binance saw a spike in withdrawals after returning online following the $6.3 billion heist.
